title: Power Stations with a Past
paragraphs: Inside almost every cell in your body are tiny structures called mitochondria. They are often described as the power stations of the cell, because they use oxygen and nutrients from food to produce a molecule called ATP, which supplies energy for most cellular activities. Cells that work especially hard, such as those in muscles and the heart, depend heavily on them. Mature red blood cells are an exception, because they have none.

Mitochondria are unusual in another way: they carry their own small set of DNA, separate from the main genetic material in the cell nucleus. This clue supports a remarkable idea known as the endosymbiotic theory. According to it, mitochondria descend from free-living bacteria that were taken inside another cell more than a billion years ago. Instead of being digested, the bacteria stayed and became permanent partners. The American biologist Lynn Margulis became its best known champion, at a time when many scientists still doubted it.

In humans, mitochondrial DNA is usually inherited from the mother alone. When mitochondria do not work properly, the organs that need the most energy, such as the brain and muscles, are often the first to suffer.

sources.claim: Mitokondriler hücre enerjisinin %90'ından fazlasını üretir; en yaygın hücresel enerji kaynağı olan ATP'yi oluştururlar; olgun kırmızı kan hücreleri dışındaki her hücre mitokondri içerir.
sources.source: National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIH), Mitochondria; https://www.nigms.nih.gov/node/144581

sources.claim: Mitokondrilerin çekirdekteki kromozomlardan ayrı, kendi küçük DNA'sı vardır; bozuklukları en çok beyin, kas ve kalp gibi yüksek enerji gerektiren dokuları etkiler.
Yumurta hücresi mitokondri katar, sperm katmaz; mtDNA kaynaklı durumlar yalnızca anneden kalıtılır.
sources.source: MedlinePlus Genetics, Mitochondrial complex V deficiency (maternal inheritance of mtDNA); https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/mitochondrial-complex-v-deficiency/

sources.claim: Endosimbiyotik hipoteze göre mitokondriler bakteriyel kökenlidir; olay yaklaşık 1,45 milyar yıl önce gerçekleşmiştir (bakteri konak hücre tarafından içe alınmıştır).
sources.source: PMC (NIH), Independent and sensory human mitochondrial functions reflecting symbiotic evolution; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10302212/

sources.claim: Lynn Margulis (Amerikalı biyolog) endosimbiyoz kuramını savundu; ilk makalesi onlarca dergi tarafından reddedildi ve eleştiri sert oldu.
